product.olivetti-m200.summary: Olivetti’s compact desktop combining monitor and drives in a fixed assembly for MS-DOS work.
product.olivetti-m200.history: The M200 was already being presented as a new Olivetti PC in December 1988: the CERN staff bulletin announced a demonstration for the 7th. Its compact design attached the monitor to the computer body. In February 1989, Piccadilly Micros offered it in the UK for £999 excluding VAT and carriage, with 640 KB, a 20 MB disk, monochrome monitor, keyboard and MS-DOS. It was priced below the M240 and M290 in that same advertisement. These dates establish its presence and an offering, not an exact launch date. Sources: CERN bulletin 49/88, p. IV; Personal Computer World, February 1989, Piccadilly Micros advertisement; Amedeo Valoroso’s observation of the machine.
product.olivetti-m200.warning: Historical research sheet: no BIOS attributed to the M200 or creation platform in BluMach.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.identity: The monitor is part of the assembly and determines its layout. The BU 200-X unit documented by Valoroso uses a DSM 200 display; the Museo del Calcolatore describes it as a 12-inch monochrome screen. The 8 MHz NEC V40 CPU also appears in the February 1989 Computer Express advertisement.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.memory: The sources disagree on available memory. The 1989 advertisements and Valoroso’s inspection report 640 KB; the latter describes soldered RAM. Olivrea lists 1024 KB for BU 200-X. Both values are retained without treating 1024 KB as a confirmed upgrade or maximum.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.storage: It was sold with different drive combinations. Personal Computer World advertises one M200 with twin floppies and another with a 20 MB disk. Valoroso identifies a 3.5-inch 720 KB drive and an optional second drive; Olivrea lists 1.44 MB. The discrepancy remains open until the manual and original drives can be checked.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.video: The integrated screen displays PC graphics without a separate monitor. Valoroso documents CGA compatibility, 80 × 25 text and 640 × 200 graphics; the video circuit remains unidentified. Sharing a CPU with Prodest PC 1 does not establish use of its Yamaha V6355.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.ports: Cards and peripherals extend the machine’s capabilities. Valoroso observes two 8-bit ISA slots on a separate board, DB25 serial and parallel ports and an AT keyboard through a five-pin DIN connector. The internal 44-pin disk connector alone does not identify its protocol.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.firmware: A startup screen identifies the diagnostics but cannot replace a dump. Valoroso documents Resident Diagnostics and the message “ROM BASIC not available” when no boot medium is found. No M200 BIOS has yet been identified among the preserved files.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.etv: ROMs from a related machine are not automatically interchangeable. ETV 2900 revisions 1.01 and 1.03, each 32 KiB, are preserved as comparative material; static analysis identifies “ETV Resident Diagnostics”. They are not attributed to the M200 and have not been executed for this sheet.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.verified: Advertisements, observations of physical units and the licensed photograph have been cross-checked. BluMach contains a NEC V40 baseline for Prodest PC 1, but no M200 platform in the reviewed code. PC 1 validation is not inherited and no M200 boot test has been performed.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.limitati: The sheet cannot create or boot the machine. Its own BIOS, a technical manual and characterisation of memory, video, keyboard, disks, ports and resets are still needed. Olivrea lists the M200 manual without a download; the VintAds brochure has been located but not acquired. The RAM and floppy discrepancy remains unresolved.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.source_a: Personal Computer World, February 1989: Piccadilly Micros (PDF page 29), price and hard-disk configuration; Computer Express (page 35), 8 MHz V40, 640 KB and twin floppies. Retail prices, not launch prices.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.source_c: CERN Staff Association bulletin 49/88, 5 December 1988, p. IV: announcement of a demonstration of the new M200 for 7 December.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.source_o: Amedeo Valoroso, “Olivetti M200”: inspection and restoration of a BU 200-X unit; board, screen, memory, ports, drives and diagnostic messages.
Olivrea, “olivetti M200”: BU 200-X record with 1024 KB and a 1.44 MB floppy drive. Conflicting collection data, not confirmed specifications for every unit.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.source_p: Photograph by ValorosoIT / Amedeo Valoroso, 9 February 2025, CC BY-SA 4.0, unchanged. The pictured ANK 27-102 keyboard was not part of the original bundle, according to the author.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.source_m: Museo del Calcolatore “Laura Tellini”, M200: collection unit with integrated 12-inch monochrome monitor. Its floppy record contains inconsistent units and is not used to establish capacity.
product.olivetti-m200.technical.source_c: BluMach 88f74ba3: Prodest PC 1 initialisation and NEC V40 device; code inspection, not an M200 implementation or validation.
